llm.summary: The skill's code and manifest contain several incoherences and surprising behaviors (hard-coded API keys, execution of system commands, and references to another skill on the user's home path) that do not line up cleanly with the advertised instruction-only marketing utility — review and fix these before installing.

dimensions.detail: On the surface the files match the described purpose (multi-platform content analysis, title/script generation, memory storage). However there are mismatches: the package includes a scripts/config.js with API keys embedded even though manifest/env metadata declare no required env vars and SKILL.md instructs users to run a config command. The presence of video-integration code that invokes an external local skill is plausible for a marketing hub, but it introduces cross-skill filesystem execution that is not obviously documented in the README/SKILL.md or manifest.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code go beyond simple API calls and text generation: marketing_hub.js will write/overwrite scripts/config.js (storing tokens on disk), call external binaries (curl via child_process, start/ensure Xvfb, run google-chrome), and may execute another skill's script at a hard-coded path (~/.openclaw-agent2/.../run_render.py) if present. SKILL.md suggests cloning from GitHub and configuring tokens; the code, however, already contains tokens and will attempt browser scraping/search modes that spawn system processes. These behaviors expand scope to local filesystem access and arbitrary subprocess execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but README/SKILL.md instructs users to git clone the GitHub repo. The package already contains the source files. There are no opaque external download URLs in the manifest, so install risk is moderate — the real risk comes from runtime exec of system binaries (Xvfb, google-chrome, curl) rather than the installer itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Manifest declares no required env vars, but the code expects two API credentials (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). Worse: scripts/config.js bundled with the skill contains apparent live API keys (including a key prefixed with 'sk-'), i.e., hard-coded secrets delivered in the package. This is inconsistent and risky: the skill both requests no declared credentials and ships credentials in plaintext. The code also uses DEEPSEEK_KEY directly in a shell-invoked curl command (exposes secret to process table).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest permits reading/writing the skill's scripts and memory directories, which matches the memory system. But the code attempts to access a hard-coded path in the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...), invoking a script from another skill if present — this crosses skill boundaries and could execute arbitrary code outside the skill's declared roots. The script also spawns system services/commands (Xvfb, pkill, chrome) which are not limited by the manifest's declared allowed subprocess patterns (only node was specified).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key issues to consider before installing:
- The package contains plaintext API keys in scripts/config.js. Do not trust those keys — they may be leaked credentials. Prefer a version that does NOT ship secrets. If you proceed, rotate those keys immediately and never reuse them elsewhere.
- The skill's manifest declares no required env vars but the code needs TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY. Confirm with the author which credentials are required and why they were bundled.
- The code executes system commands (curl, Xvfb, google-chrome) and may start/kill Xvfb or launch Chrome. If you run this in a hosted environment, those commands may fail or have unexpected side effects. Running in a sandboxed environment is recommended.
- cmd_vid_integration.py references and will attempt to run a script at ~/.openclaw-agent2/.../run_render.py. That means the skill may call into other locally installed skills or arbitrary files in your home directory. If you do not want cross-skill execution, remove or review that integration first.
- child_process exec/execSync usage constructs shell commands as strings (not arrays), which can lead to shell injection if an untrusted value reaches these commands. Inspect inputs you pass to the skill and avoid passing untrusted strings.
- Ask the maintainer to: (1) remove hard-coded keys from the repo, (2) declare required env vars in the manifest, (3) avoid or document cross-skill hard-coded paths, and (4) replace shell-string execs with safer exec variants or parameterized calls.
- If you still want to test it: run it in an isolated VM/container, remove the bundled keys, and inspect runtime network calls (only api.tikhub.io and api.deepseek.com are listed as allowed hosts in manifest). If you see calls to unexpected endpoints or any unexpected local script execution, stop and investigate.
